page: Microsoft Azure E16-8ads_v7 is a constrained-CPU memory-optimized virtual machine instance running on Microsoft Hyper-V. The system is provisioned with 8 dedicated vCPUs (4 physical cores across 2 threads per core) derived from an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor clocked at up to 4.5 GHz. It includes 48 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache per core cluster, with instruction set extensions such as AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, AVX-512 BF16, AES, VAES, and SHA-NI. The instance pairs this compute core count with 128.0 GB of system memory, providing a high ratio of 16.0 GB RAM per vCPU, as well as 944 GB of direct-attached NVMe SSD local storage.

Benchmark results highlight strong single-core efficiency, with the AMD EPYC core scoring in the top tier on both stress-ng single-core (3,787.58) and Geekbench single-core (2,774.0). Single-threaded tasks such as gzip compression (41.57 GB/sec) and bzip3 decompression (18.37 GB/sec) also test in the top tier, matching the high 4.5 GHz clock profile. Conversely, overall multithreaded capacity is bound by the 8 vCPU limit, reflecting middle-tier performance on PassMark CPU (19,052.76), Geekbench multi-core (10,407.0), and stress-ng multi-core (15,180.55).

Memory throughput registers at 50.01 GB/sec for large block uncached reads and 34.09 GB/sec for uncached writes, driving solid database operations with Redis SET executing at 14.99 million operations per second. For machine learning tasks without dedicated GPU hardware, small language model text generation achieves strong throughput at 296.96 tokens per second, though larger 7B model prompt processing falls into the bottom tier at 31.51 tokens per second due to core constraints.

The constrained configuration offers significant cost efficiency for workloads that are memory-intensive or I/O-heavy but licensed per CPU core. By providing 128 GB of RAM and fast NVMe storage over only 8 vCPUs, it reduces core-based software licensing costs while preventing compute overprovisioning. The E16-8ads_v7 is particularly well suited for in-memory caching layers, relational databases like SQL Server or Oracle requiring high memory-to-core ratios, and intermediate analytics jobs.
description: Microsoft Azure E16-8ads_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine offering 8 dedicated vCPUs from an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor capable of 4.5 GHz, 128.0 GB of memory, and 944 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. Operating under Microsoft Hyper-V, the instance features an architecture tailored for high memory-per-core allocation at 16.0 GB per vCPU. Benchmark evaluations show top-tier single-threaded performance, with Geekbench single-core reaching 2,774.0 and gzip compression achieving 41.57 GB/sec, alongside middle-tier multithreaded results reflecting the 8-vCPU physical boundary. Memory bandwidth reaches 50.01 GB/sec on uncached reads, supporting 14.99 million Redis SET operations per second. This instance maximizes efficiency for software licensed on a per-core basis that demands elevated RAM and local disk performance, including relational database engines, large caching tiers, and memory-bound transactional workloads.
